title: Lsp2 links early-life diet to adult translation and lifespan in Drosophila
title_zh: Lsp2 将幼年饮食与果蝇成年翻译活性及寿命关联
abstract: Abstract Nearly a century ago, restricting diet during early-life periods was suggested to extend lifespan in rats and in Daphnia 1,2 . The effect of juvenile diet on adult physiology and lifespan has subsequently been described in other model organisms, including fruit flies 3–5 and mice 6–8 ; however, its mechanism remains poorly understood. Here, using Drosophila as a model, we show that restricting protein intake during the larval stage (early-life protein restriction; ePR) promotes adult lifespan by reducing the levels of storage proteins. Using stable-isotope tracing, we show that dietary amino acids obtained in the larval stage are retained into early adulthood, and are incorporated into ribosomal proteins in particular. This is mediated by larval serum protein 2 (Lsp2), a major storage protein, the expression of which is durably downregulated by ePR in the early adult stage. Genetic silencing of Lsp2 phenocopies ePR, attenuating ribosomal-protein abundance and translational activity in early adulthood, and extending lifespan. Restricting specific amino acids that are especially enriched in these storage proteins, such as phenylalanine and tyrosine, is sufficient to decrease the levels of early-life Lsp2 and promote longevity. These findings identify Lsp2 as a molecular carrier of nutritional history across developmental transitions, linking juvenile nutritional status to adult translational capacity and lifespan. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism of nutritional memory that links early-life diet to lifelong organismal health.
abstract_zh: 摘要：近一个世纪前，限制幼年期饮食被认为能延长大鼠和淡水虾的寿命1,2。随后在其他模式生物中也描述了幼年饮食对成年生理和寿命的影响，包括果蝇3–5和小鼠6–8；但其机制尚不清楚。本文以果蝇为模型，发现幼虫期限制蛋白摄入（早期蛋白限制；ePR）通过降低储存蛋白水平来延长成年寿命。利用稳定同位素追踪显示，幼虫期摄入的饮食氨基酸在成年早期被保留，并特别被整合到核糖体蛋白中。这一过程由幼虫血清蛋白2（Lsp2）介导，Lsp2是一种主要的储存蛋白，其表达在成年早期被ePR持续下调。对Lsp2进行基因沉默可模拟ePR，降低成年早期核糖体蛋白丰度和翻译活性，并延长寿命。限制富含在这些储存蛋白中的特定氨基酸，如苯丙氨酸和酪氨酸，足以降低早期Lsp2水平并促进长寿。这些发现将Lsp2确定为跨发育转变的营养史分子载体，将幼年营养状态与成年翻译能力和寿命联系起来。我们的研究揭示了一种此前未被认识到的营养记忆机制，将早期饮食与终身生物体健康相连。
